summary: The design, outcomes, schedule, factors, token ceiling, and scoring remained sealed, but model-facing serialization compatibility fixes were made after early prediction checkpoints. Existing checkpoints were never replaced.

events.event: A stale service drop-in selected Qwen3-4B. The run stopped before prediction and the drop-in was reversibly disabled so the declared Qwen3-8B configuration loaded.
A long thinking generation crossed WSL idle teardown and rebooted the guest. A non-model-facing WSL anchor was added; the failed condition had no checkpoint and was retried.
This llama.cpp build rejected object-form named tool_choice. Terminal serialization changed to supported required mode with only the recorder exposed.
The recorder schema allowed duplicate rank integers although the validator required permutations. uniqueItems was added to both rank arrays; the rejected condition had no checkpoint.
A truncated reasoning-only message left an open think block when replayed. Such thoughts are now retained externally but omitted from the clean reasoning-disabled serialization prompt.
Malformed autonomous recorder JSON was found to be unreplayable by llama.cpp. It is counted and retained externally, then the unchanged evidence is sent to the clean recorder-only fallback.

invariants_preserved: No rejected response received a prediction checkpoint.
No sealed prediction was regenerated or replaced.
No causal outcome, correctness feedback, or controller-computed answer entered a model request.
All scored requests used Qwen3-8B, temperature zero, and a 1024-token ceiling.
The source artifact, schedule, exact rule text, factor assignment, and scoring remained unchanged.
interpretation: The batch is valuable localization evidence and all exact requests are auditable, but implementation-version imbalance prevents describing its p-values as a clean final confirmatory test. A successor must freeze and dry-run the final serializer before prediction 1.
